newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab League says tunnel is attack on Islamic sites.
newsitem.headline: Arab League says tunnel is attack on Islamic sites.

text.p: The Arab League warned on Tuesday that Israel had enraged Moslems worldwide by opening a Jerusalem tunnel near Islam's third holiest site and risked triggering widespread unrest.
Palestinians clashed with police in Jerusalem on Tuesday after Israeli workmen opened the tunnel under cover of night and heavy police guard.
Israel says opening the tunnel will give tourists easier access to archaeological sites beneath the Wailing Wall, Judaism's holiest site.

"The Secretariat of the Arab League warns of the consequences of such action and ensuing feelings of anger and increased levels of tension and angry popular confrontation," the Cairo-based league said in a statement.

"The Arab League will turn to the United Nations, the co-sponsors of the peace process and to the European Union to immediately and seriously try to persuade Israel to stop this work, which undoubtedly will stir the feelings of Moslems all over the world," it added.

The league said the tunnel was the latest attempt by the Jewish state to eliminate Arab and Islamic monuments in the disputed city. Israel annexed Arab East Jerusalem after capturing it in the Middle East war of 1967.
Palestinians want East Jerusalem for the capital of their future state but Israel claims the whole city as its "eternal capital".

"The Arab League is following with anger what the Israeli occupation authorities are doing to...wipe out its Arab and Islamic sites and its continuing attacks on the blessed al-Aqsa mosque," the league said.

"The Arab League affirms that such actions represent a clear attack on Islamic holy sites and a violation of the Geneva Convention and the U.N. Security Council resolutions on the Arab-Israeli dispute and the Palestinian issue," it added.
The league said Israel was also violating its agreements with the Palestinians, which referred issues related to Jerusalem to final status negotiations between the two sides.
